blocks.value: People invest because they want their money to grow faster than inflation. There is no single investment that is best for everyone.

Imagine five friends each have ₹10,000. One keeps it in a bank, another buys gold, another invests in mutual funds, another buys shares, and another starts a small business. After several years, each investment performs differently.
Some common investment options include Fixed Deposits (FDs), Gold, Real Estate, Mutual Funds, Stocks, Government Bonds, and starting your own business.
Each investment has different levels of risk, return, and time commitment. Learning these differences helps you make better financial decisions.
The stock market is just one of many investment options. Throughout this course, we'll understand why many investors choose it for long-term wealth creation.
